A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AICrypto study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization and added examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 17 LLM configurations on MCQs, CTF challenges, and proof problems, alongside collected human MCQ results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original model evaluations and reports revised human MCQ results and additional model-response examples.

M1.justification: The CTF agent retains the same interaction loop, four available actions, helper scripts, and flag-verification procedure. Moving framework details into Appendix C and displaying additional trajectories does not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 135 MCQs, 150 CTF challenges, and 18 proof problems from three exams. The 73 static and 77 dynamic CTF challenges and represented cryptographic topics remain unchanged. Additional appendix examples come from retained coverage.

E2.justification: The same 17 model configurations and human baseline groups participate in the corresponding MCQ, CTF, and proof comparisons. Newly cited related benchmarks are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The human MCQ time allowance changes from 8 hours in v1 Section 3.2 to 12 hours in v3 Appendix D.1. This is a reported protocol revision, without an explicit account of reruns. Model versions, token budgets, task metrics, and the 100-action CTF limit remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices F–G substantially expand inspectable case-study evidence with Gemini static and dynamic successes, a failure involving repeated timeouts, and four scored proof responses. These replace or extend v1's compact success illustrations and single worked proof. Most existing failure examples and the iteration analysis are retained elsewhere.

E5.justification: Both report three independent CTF attempts with pass@3 and the same human averaging practices. Neither adds seed specifications, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Figure 2 changes human mean MCQ accuracy from 77.5% to 91.9% and the human composite score from 246.8 to 261.1, under the revised time allowance. Aggregate LLM scores remain unchanged. Additional case outcomes are reported, and v1's incorrect claim that o4-mini-high exceeds o3 on proofs is removed; their retained scores are 62.1% and 77.6%, respectively.

T1.justification: v1 Figure 12's worked proof that no universal hardcore bit exists is removed. v3 Appendix G adds explicit PRG/PRF counterexample derivations and unsuccessful OWF-composition proof attempts. This changes the illustrative formal content without introducing theoretical guarantees for the benchmark or agent.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a comprehensive cryptography benchmark, an agent-based CTF evaluation framework, and evaluation of 17 LLMs against human references. The abstract and conclusion retain the same strengths on familiar tasks and weaknesses in deeper mathematical and dynamic reasoning.

C2.justification: v3 drops the inference that correlated proof and CTF performance indicates theoretical understanding aids practical solving, and removes the specialization/fatigue qualification of human scores. It also removes the detailed future-application discussion. The principal failure explanations and limitations concerning grading automation and agent-framework scope remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a direct repository pointer and identifies the PhD students responsible for proof grading. Most model, hardware, software, and prompt details are retained. However, v1's explicit command-timeout rule—300 seconds for short reference solutions, otherwise five times reference runtime—is no longer documented.

R1.justification: v3 adds CipherBank (Li et al., 2025), distinguishing its classical-decryption scope, and Yang et al. (2025) on numerical reasoning robustness. The broader related-work coverage and comprehensive-cryptography positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: The introduction, methods, and results are substantially condensed and reorganized. Human evaluation, framework details, and detailed analyses move into expanded appendices; the standalone discussion section disappears. Ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-usage statements are added, alongside extensive paragraph and heading revisions.

P2.justification: v3 relocates the MCQ heatmap and file-structure diagram, interleaves humans within the MCQ ranking, abbreviates heatmap labels, and redraws the iteration plot. It adds extensive color-coded transcript figures and new proof-example displays, removes earlier illustrations, and abridges the displayed MCQ example.

improvement.justification: The added CTF transcripts and scored proof responses make the central capability diagnoses easier to inspect, and v3 removes the erroneous o4-mini-high versus o3 proof-ranking statement. These provide a limited quality gain, tempered by the loss of the explicit command-timeout rule and human-baseline caveat. The benchmark and aggregate LLM evidence remain stable.
